title: Multi-variant aliasing + tenant-sticky routing for safe embedding model roll-ins
creator: Rafael Ortega
description:
Goal: Build a safe, observable onboarding path for new embedding models and variants that minimizes user-visible regressions while preserving low-latency serving for the reranking/embedding endpoints. Scope covers: aliasing semantics for model variants, tenant-scoped sticky routing, contract checks (dimensionality/quantization/tokenizer compatibility), soft-traffic ramps, shadow testing against rerank benchmarks, and rollout automation hooks for Console and API.

Motivation: Recent embedding swaps highlighted risks: silent semantics drift for tenant-specific corpora, dimension/key-mismatch errors in downstream rerank pipelines, and latency regressions when new quantized variants are selected. We need a standardized, rollback-capable path that platform engineers and PMs can use to introduce new variants with measurable quality and latency signals.

High-level design summary:
- Alias layer: expose model aliases (e.g., embeddings/sim-small -> variant v1,v2) that map to one or more serving variants. Aliases present a stable contract to customers while routing can be changed under the hood.
- Multi-variant routing: support probabilistic split and sticky tenant pinning so each tenant can be routed consistently to a variant during a rollout window.
- Contract probes: pre-acceptance checks for dimension, dtype, tokenizer compatibility, and offline semantic stability on a per-tenant sample (where available).
- Shadow rerank harness: run inference through candidate variant in shadow mode for a subset of traffic and compute rerank delta metrics (NDCG@k, cosine shift distributions, embedding drift) without affecting live responses.
- Latency guardrails: enforce per-variant SLO budgets (p95/p99) and automatic fallback to alias baseline variant if tail latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.
- Quantization compatibility matrix: annotate variants with quantization profile and required runtime kernel features; autoskip variants on hardware lacking proper kernels.
- Observability: per-alias dashboards (Console) showing quality delta, latency distribution, token cost delta, and tenant adoption map.

Non-goals: full model training pipeline, retrieval/index migration, or long-lived dataset storage for tenant probes (we will rely on short sampled payloads or customer-provided canary datasets).
acceptance_criteria: Alias API accepts creation of multi-variant alias and returns a stable alias id
Tenant-sticky routing persists assignment for the duration of the rollout window and honors per-tenant overrides in Console
Shadow rerank runs for at least 5% of traffic on a canary cohort and reporting shows NDCG/embedding-drift comparisons
Automatic latency fallback triggers when variant p99 > baseline p99 + 40ms or error rate increases > 1% for a 5-minute window
Contract probe rejects variant if embedding dimensionality or tokenizer vocabulary mismatch is detected
Console dashboard displays per-tenant adoption, quality delta, latency delta, and provides a single-click rollback
End-to-end smoke PRs merged and e2e tests added to CI validating alias routing and fallback behaviors
comments: 2026-03-01 Rafael Ortega: Created ticket after postmortem for EMB-SWAP-3. Proposed alias + tenant pinning approach; sketched metrics to track. Filing for engineering implementation and PM review.

2026-03-03 Aisha Kumar: Spike completed — validated sticky assignment using existing tenant metadata store. Found that current tenant lookup has 200ms median additional latency when called synchronously; plan to move to async lookup cached in edge routing layer.

2026-03-04 Jun Park (review): Raised concern about dimension mismatches for legacy customers with proprietary embedding adapters. Recommended adding a preflight 'contract-check' API call customers can invoke before switching alias targets.
2026-03-06 PM review (Lena Brooks): Approved plan pending telemetry dashboards and clear rollback UX in Console. Suggested including cost delta estimate for quantized vs. float variants.

2026-03-08 Infra (Marta Silva): Noted kernel compatibility gap on older GPU fleet for q4-bit quantized variants. Added dependency to ENG-395123 to gate rollout until selective routing by hardware is implemented.

2026-03-09 Aisha Kumar: Implemented prototype alias mapping and tenant assignment persistence. Opened GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8142 — includes unit tests for routing logic.

2026-03-10 Rafael Ortega: Deployed shadow harness to a staging cluster and ran the rerank benchmark suite against new variant (v2). Observed NDCG drop of 0.8% on public benchmark, but per-tenant drift varied widely — plan to add tenant-level fence for semantic regressions.
